newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria refinery cuts volumes to critical minimum.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria refinery cuts volumes to critical minimum.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim has cut oil volumes to the critical minimum due to a lack of cash for crude supplies, refinery officials said on Monday.

"Neftohim has been refining just 6,500 tonnes of crude per day since Friday from 8,000 tonnes last week and distributes 1,000 tonnes of petrol per day for the domestic market," plant spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said by telephone from Bourgas.
Hadzhieva said a private firm Yucos Petroleum Bulgaria had promised to supply a tanker of Russian crude and it was expected to arrive in the Black Sea port of Bourgas on Wednesday.
Petar Tsanov, deputy director of the biggest state-owned fuel retailer, Petrol, told Reuters that 99 percent of their 450 filling stations were closed because of a lack of gasoline.
"We received only 430 tonnes of gasoline and 106 tonnes of diesel for all our petrol stations for the last three days from Friday until Sunday," Tsanov said.

Bulgaria, which has not suffered such petrol shortages since 1990, was paralysed by a lack of petrol over the weekend. Municipalities continue distributing petrol and diesel mainly for ambulances, police, army, fire brigades and food suppliers. Radio stations in Sofia warned people that city transport was running a reduced service due to the fuel shortage.
Regular government revisions of fuel prices have not kept up with a recent drastic fall of the lev against the dollar.
Refinery officials said a tonne of gasoline on the domestic market cost now $60 while its price was more than $200 on the international market.
The Bulgarian lev traded at 3,100-3,150 per dollar on the interbank market on Monday.
Financial weekly newspaper Kapital said the refinery now owed more than $300 million to crude suppliers.

Neftohim's management is now seeking credits from foreign lending institutions to survive until the end of the year, refinery officials said. But the country does not have an efficient government yet to guarantee such a loan, they added.
Russia's state-owned Rosneft oil company said last week it had reduced crude oil supplies to Neftohim because of unpaid debts.
A tanker left Russia's Odessa port last week heading for Neftohim but diverted to another destination, probably after receiving an offer from a more creditworthy client, officials said.
